title: Are there more ways to glue four cubes?
description: Five flat ways of gluing four cubes are known. The board lifts the fourth cube off the table in different places, finds the tripod and two mirror image screws, and counts eight ways in all.
teaching_notes: One idea: a new way to glue four cubes must lift one cube out of the flat plane, and the place where it sits gives a different shape. Watch for students who count a shape and its mirror image as the same.

video_script.why: The child finds the shapes of four glued cubes that do not lie flat by lifting the fourth cube in different places.
video_script.substitution: Lift the fourth cube off the table and place it on a different cube each time.
video_script.anchor: an L of three cubes lying flat on a table, a fourth cube in hand, and a grid to draw each shape on
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, there are three more, the tripod and two mirror image screws, making eight ways in all

final_answer.value: Yes: 3 more, the tripod and two mirror image screws, for 8 ways in all
final_answer.spoken: yes, three more, the tripod and two mirror image screws, for eight ways in all

hold_back: Answer: Yes: 3 more, the tripod and two mirror image screws, for 8 ways in all
never_show: a flat shape marked as a new way
maths_rules: the 5 known ways lie flat; a new way must lift one cube off the plane
L of 3 cubes with the 4th cube on top of the corner cube: 3 arms meet at a corner, the tripod
L of 3 cubes with the 4th cube on top of an end cube: a screw; the other end gives its mirror image screw
video_script.design: An L of three cubes sits on a grid. The fourth cube is placed on the corner cube, then on one end, then on the other end, and each shape is turned and drawn on the grid.
open_questions: The worklist describes the screw as an S shape with one end lifted. The video builds it as an L of three cubes with the fourth cube on top of an end cube, which is the same shape.
